report: The patient's acute symmetrical lower-limb weakness is best explained by hyperkalemia-related weakness. Initial serum potassium was 6.94 mmol/L with peaked T waves, confirming severe hyperkalemia; serial levels normalized to 4.57–4.68 mmol/L, ruling out pseudo-hyperkalemia. Hyperkalemia directly impairs muscle membrane excitability, producing symmetrical weakness. Hypokalemia is refuted by hyperkalemia and normalization without hypokalemia. Functional, medication-induced, and neuromuscular causes lack objective support and cannot explain the metabolic disturbance. The historical hypokalemic, KCl-responsive episodes remain unexplained, so confidence is moderate, but the current episode is most consistent with hyperkalemia-related weakness.

The 14-day Zio monitor documented a 4.5-second ventricular pause with junctional escape and dual sinus node activity, supporting CAV-related arrhythmia as the cause of symptoms in this post-transplant patient with grade 1 CAV. Medication-related hypotension is secondary given normotensive exam and pause despite amlodipine cessation. Autonomic dysregulation is less supported. Missing coronary/IVUS, medication/electrolyte, biopsy/echo data prevent excluding reversible causes, so confidence is 0.70.
